classification.difficultyReason: Use a supplementary ratio equation and propagate all eight angles with named reasons.

content.prompt:
$AB$ is parallel to $CD$ and $PQRS$ is a transversal.

If $y=3x$, find the size of all angles, giving reasons.

spec.description: Two oblique parallel lines A–Q–B and C–R–D rise rightwards. A vertical transversal contains P–Q–R–S. Single rightward parallel chevrons lie on QB and RD. The acute sector PQB contains x; the obtuse sector DRS contains y. Unshaded black geometry.
spec.mathematics: A,Q,B are collinear; C,R,D are collinear; P,Q,R,S are collinear in that order; AB is parallel to CD. The displayed angles x and y are supplementary.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given angle labels x and y are visible; numerical answers are solution-only.

answer.short:
$\angle PQB=\angle AQR=\angle QRD=\angle CRS=45^\circ$.

$\angle PQA=\angle BQR=\angle QRC=\angle DRS=135^\circ$.

Thus $x=45^\circ$ and $y=135^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$\angle PQB=\angle QRD=x$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines).

$\angle QRD+\angle DRS=180^\circ$ (angles on the straight line $QRS$).

$$\begin{align*}x+3x&=180^\circ\\4x&=180^\circ\\x&=45^\circ\\y&=3\times45^\circ\\y&=135^\circ\end{align*}$$

Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $\angle AQR=\angle CRS=45^\circ$ and $\angle QRC=135^\circ$.

Angles on the straight line $PQR$ give $\angle BQR=135^\circ$. Its vertically opposite angle is $\angle PQA=135^\circ$.
